auto.notice: <!-- This section is generated by Agentuino. Changes here will be overwritten. -->
auto.ruleSketch: - This is an Arduino sketch. Do not rename the folder or the main file `{0}`.
auto.ruleScope: - Work only inside this sketch folder.
auto.ruleSrc: - Additional code files (.h, .cpp) belong in the sketch folder or in `src/`, otherwise they are not compiled.
auto.ruleMemory: - Read `{0}` first. Only record what applies beyond this conversation: parts, wiring, decisions, solved problems. No conversation logs, those are in the chat protocols.
auto.ruleBeginner: - The user is a beginner: explain briefly and clearly what you do and why.
auto.boardUnknown: - Board: not detected. Ask the user which board they use.
auto.compile: Compile after every code change and fix errors on your own:
auto.upload: Upload only when the user explicitly asks for it:
auto.uploadAuto: Upload after every successful compile, without asking (anchor "Upload automatically"):
auto.knowledgeIntro: Read these files when they are relevant to the task:
auto.ruleNoUpload: - NEVER upload the sketch to the board on your own, not even after a successful compile. The board may control motors, relays or other hardware.
auto.portHint: The port is unknown. Find it with `{0}`. If there are several candidates, ask the user.
auto.chatsIntro: Earlier conversations about this project are stored as protocols in `{0}`. If the user refers to an earlier conversation or you lack background, search them specifically with Grep for keywords and read only the matching parts. Never read all protocols completely.
auto.ruleLibraries: - Install libraries or board packages (lib install, core install) only after asking the user. They apply to all sketches.
auto.serialIntro: This reads the serial output of the board for a few seconds (baud rate as in `Serial.begin()`, at most 60 seconds). The port is chosen automatically; with several boards, pass it with `--port`:
serialRules: - Read the serial output only with `agentuino-serial`. Do not use cat, stty, screen, Python or `arduino-cli monitor` for it: they hang, block the port or lose data.
- The sketch keeps running while you read, so the output starts in the middle and the first line may be incomplete. Whether opening the port restarts the board depends on the board.
- `--send "text"` sends a line to the sketch after the start (for `Serial.read()`). Add `--no-newline` if the sketch reads single characters, otherwise it also reads the newline as input.
- If the command reports a busy port, or nothing arrives after an upload, the Serial Monitor of the IDE probably holds the port. Ask the user to open and close it once.

- A sketch uploaded with "Optimize for Debugging" (ArduDebug) can be read like a normal one, even during a debug session. Unreadable characters usually mean a wrong baud rate: use the one from `Serial.begin()`.
auto.serialBoardCode: - You see what currently runs on the board. That is not necessarily the current code: upload only after asking, or the user uploads in the IDE.
auto.serialBoardCodeAuto: - You see what currently runs on the board. After a successful upload that is the current code.
auto.debugIntro: ArduDebug is installed. With it you stop the program on the board at a line and read variables, without changing the code. The command builds a debug build with the ArduDebug variant of the board itself:
debugRules: - Offer debugging when you look for a bug and what happens at runtime matters. Ask first whether the user wants it.

- A debug build must run on the board. If the command reports that none runs, ask the user whether you may upload one, then call the command with `--upload`. Tell the user: in a debug build pins 0, 1 and 2 (Uno, Nano) or pin 7 (Leonardo) belong to the debugger. `agentuino-debug` returns the `Serial` output of the run itself; `agentuino-serial` and the Serial Monitor work with a debug build too.
- If the sketch drives motors, heaters, relays or similar, ask before every stop: at a breakpoint the hardware stays in its state.
- At most 8 breakpoints. Breakpoints in interrupt routines are never reached. With breakpoints set the program runs slower, and while it is stopped `millis()` does not count on.

- A breakpoint on the line right after a waiting loop (e.g. `while (Serial.available() == 0);`) can be hit while the program is still waiting. Check the variables to see whether the loop was really left, or set the breakpoint one line later.

- If the sketch needs input before it reaches the place you want to inspect, pass it with `agentuino-debug --send "text"` (add `--no-newline` for single characters). Do not run `agentuino-serial` in parallel for this.

- When debugging has done its job: fix the bug in the sketch and remove everything you added only for debugging. The debug build may stay on the board. Upload the normal build with `agentuino-debug --restore` only if the user asks for it.
- Never call `ardudebug-bridge` or `avr-gdb` directly, only through `agentuino-debug`.

rules.title: ⚓ Semantic anchors
rules.noSketch: No sketch open: here you set the defaults for new sketches.
rules.intro: Checked anchors are written as rules into the project instructions (AGENTS.md) and apply from the next message on. The safety rules always apply. Only "Upload automatically" lets the agent upload on its own: use it only when the board drives nothing that could be dangerous.
rules.customHint: Custom anchors are available in all sketches.
rules.deleteConfirm: Delete the anchor "{0}"? It disappears from all sketches.
rules.saveDefaults: Save as default for new sketches
rules.defaultsSaved: Saved as default for new sketches.
rules.missing: Name and rule must not be empty.

beginnerComments.label: Beginner-friendly comments
beginnerComments.text: Comment the code for beginners: explain in short comments what each part does and why.

noMagicNumbers.label: No magic numbers
noMagicNumbers.text: No magic numbers: define pins, times and limits as named constants at the top of the sketch.

nonBlocking.label: Non-blocking
nonBlocking.text: Write non-blocking code: measure time with `millis()` instead of `delay()`, so the sketch stays responsive.

lowRam.label: Save RAM
lowRam.text: Use little RAM: small data types, no unnecessary buffers, global variables only where needed.

defensive.label: Defensive programming
defensive.text: Program defensively: check return values, sensor readings and input for plausibility and handle errors.

isrSafe.label: Interrupt-safe
isrSafe.text: Keep interrupt routines short, declare shared variables `volatile` and use neither `Serial` nor `delay()` in interrupts.

noDynamicMemory.label: No String, no malloc
noDynamicMemory.text: Do not use dynamic memory: no `String`, no `malloc` or `new`. Use fixed `char` arrays.

flashStrings.label: Texts in flash
flashStrings.text: Keep constant texts in flash with `F()` or `PROGMEM` instead of RAM.

fixedWidthTypes.label: Fixed-width types
fixedWidthTypes.text: Use fixed-width types like `uint8_t`, `int16_t` or `uint32_t` instead of `int` and `long`.

explainChanges.label: Summarize changes
explainChanges.text: At the end, briefly summarize what you changed and why.

keepStyle.label: Keep the style
keepStyle.text: Keep the formatting, indentation and naming of the existing code. Do not reformat what you do not need to change.

smallSteps.label: Small steps
smallSteps.text: Work in small steps: for larger tasks first state the plan, then implement it step by step and compile after each step.

autoUpload.label: Upload automatically
autoUpload.text: Upload automatically: after every code change that compiles without errors, upload the sketch to the board without asking and say so. Never upload while errors remain. If the port is unknown or several boards are connected, ask.
